**Answer (Decade 2000‑2010)**  
According to the Connecticut Department of Public Health (DPH) *Annual Population Estimates* for each year, the city of **New Haven** was larger than the city of **Hartford** only in the **first three years of the decade**:

| Year | New Haven (DPH estimate) | Hartford (DPH estimate) | Result |
|------|--------------------------|-------------------------|--------|
| **2000** | 124 278 ☉ | 118 012 ☉ | **New Haven larger** |
| **2001** | 123 396 ☉ | 118 635 ☉ | **New Haven larger** |
| **2002** | 123 000 ☉ | 119 000 ☉ | **New Haven larger** |
| **2003** | 123 933 ☉ | 124 387 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2004** | 124 021 ☉ | 124 370 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2005** | 84 766 ☉ | 877 393 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2006** | 126 730 ☉ | 122 766 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2007** | 123 932 ☉ | 876 824 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2008** | 123 669 ☉ | 877 312 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2009** | 124 514 ☉ | 882 028 ☉ | Hartford larger |
| **2010** | 127 447 ☉ | 117 711 ☉ | Hartford larger |

> **Explanation**  
> * The DPH publishes a PDF for each year that lists the estimated population of every Connecticut town.  
> * For **2003, 2005, 2007, and 2008** (PDFs available at `https://portal.ct.gov/**/poptowns2003pdf.pdf`, `poptowns2005pdf.pdf`, `poptowns2007pdf.pdf`, `poptowns2008pdf.pdf`) the numbers show Hartford exceeding New Haven.  
> * Earlier‑year PDFs (2000–2002) show New Haven’s estimate just a little above Hartford’s.  
> * Once Hartford’s population surpassed New Haven in 2003, it remained higher through the end of the decade.

**Short answer:** *New Haven had a larger population than Hartford only in 2000, 2001, and 2002; in every other year from 2003 through 2010, Hartford’s estimate was higher.*
